settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with cross-learning, stochastic rewards and adversarial contexts
unmapped: cross-learning between contexts: playing arm i in context c reveals r_{i,t}(c') for all c' in O_i(c), given by a known per-action directed graph G_i over the C contexts (with self-loops)
the learner knows the cross-learning graphs G_i
finite set of C contexts; comparator is the best stationary policy (mapping contexts to arms) by mean reward
settings.definition_quote: for every action $i \in [K]$, we specify a directed graph $G_i$ over the set of contexts $[C]$. An edge $c \rightarrow c'$ in $G_i$ indicates that playing action $i$ in context $c$, reveals the reward of action $i$ in context $c'$. ... every reward $r_{i,t}(c)$ is drawn independently from an unknown distribution $\F_i(c)$ supported on $[0,1]$. Importantly, this algorithm works even when the contexts are chosen adversarially

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with cross-learning, adversarial rewards and stochastic contexts with known distribution
unmapped: cross-learning between contexts via known per-action directed graphs G_i over the C contexts
the learner knows the cross-learning graphs G_i
comparator is the ex-ante best stationary policy pi(c)=argmax_i sum_t r_{i,t}(c), not the best in hindsight on realized contexts
settings.definition_quote: Here, we consider contextual bandits problem with cross learning when the rewards are adversarially chosen but contexts are stochastically drawn from some distribution $\D$. ... in the first setting, the learner knows the distribution over contexts $\D$

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with cross-learning, adversarial rewards and stochastic contexts with unknown distribution
unmapped: cross-learning between contexts via a single known directed graph G (same for all actions) over the C contexts
the learner knows the cross-learning graph G
comparator is the ex-ante best stationary policy
settings.definition_quote: Consider the contextual bandits problem with adversarial rewards, and stochastic contexts, where all the CL graphs $G_i$ are equal to $G$ and the context distribution $\cal D$ is unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with complete cross-learning, adversarial rewards and adversarial contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: complete cross-learning: playing an arm reveals its reward under every context
comparator is the best stationary policy in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: There exists a distribution over instances of the contextual bandit problem with complete cross-learning where any algorithm must incur a regret of at least $\Omega(\sqrt{CKT})$.

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with cross-learning, stochastic rewards and stochastic contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: cross-learning between contexts via a fixed known directed graph G (same for all actions) over the C contexts
settings.definition_quote: Any learning algorithm solving the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning (for a fixed CL graph $G$) and stochastic rewards and stochastic contexts must incur expected regret of $\Omega(\sqrt{\nu_2(G)KT})$

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual bandits with cross-learning, stochastic rewards and adversarial contexts (lower bound)
unmapped: cross-learning between contexts via a fixed known directed graph G (same for all actions) over the C contexts
settings.definition_quote: Any learning algorithm solving the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning (for a fixed CL graph $G$) with stochastic rewards and adversarial contexts must incur regret $\Omega(\sqrt{\lambda(G)KT})$

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial rewards and stochastic contexts, ex post regret (lower bound)
unmapped: regret measured against the ex post best stationary policy in hindsight on realized contexts
settings.definition_quote: Under adversarial rewards and stochastic contexts, for any algorithm $\cal A$, there is an instance of the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning where $\liminf_{C\rightarrow \infty} \E[\Reg_{\post}(\cal A)] \geq T/2$.

settings.name_in_paper: Learning to bid in first-price auctions (single value)
unmapped: bids in [0,1]; reward (v-b)*1(b >= h_t) with highest competing bid h_t i.i.d. from unknown distribution; bidder only learns whether it wins (non-transparent auction)
settings.definition_quote: Any algorithm must incur $\Omega(T^{2/3})$ regret for the learning to bid in first price auctions problem, even if the value of the bidder is fixed (i.e., there is only one context).

symbols.kappa_bar: average over actions of the clique covering number kappa(G_i) of the cross-learning graphs

conditions: Delta^* = min over arms and contexts of mu^*(c) - mu_i(c) > 0

source.label: thm:ucbcross
source.quote: Let $\Delta^* = \min_{i\in [K], c\in [C]} (\mu^{{\star}}(c) - \mu_i(c))>0$ ... Then, \ucbcross{} (Algorithm \ref{alg:UCB1PC}) has an expected gap-dependent regret of $O\left(\frac{K\bar \kappa \log T}{\Delta^*}\right)$ and an expected gap-independent regret of $O(\sqrt{\overline{\kappa}KT\log T})$ ... in the setting with stochastic rewards and adversarial contexts

results.notes: Delta^* is the minimum gap over all suboptimal (arm, context) pairs; mapped to Delta_min. Regret defined through gaps times pull counts, hence pseudo-regret. Also covers stochastic contexts.

symbols.kappa_bar: average over actions of the clique covering number kappa(G_i) of the cross-learning graphs

source.label: thm:ucbcross
source.quote: \ucbcross{} ... has ... an expected gap-independent regret of $O(\sqrt{\overline{\kappa}KT\log T})$ for the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning in the setting with stochastic rewards and adversarial contexts

results.notes: With complete cross-learning kappa_bar=1 giving O(sqrt(KT log T)); with no cross-learning kappa_bar = C. Gap-independent results hold without unique-optimal-policy assumption.

symbols.lambda_bar: average over actions of the maximum acyclic subgraph number lambda(G_i) of the cross-learning graphs

conditions: T >= K log K (footnote in proof)
tuning: alpha = beta = sqrt(log K / (lambda_bar K T))

source.label: thm:exppcross
source.quote: \expcrossk{} (Algorithm \ref{alg:exp3PC}) has regret $O(\sqrt{\overline{\lambda}KT\log K})$ for the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning when rewards are adversarial and contexts are stochastic, where $\bar{\lambda} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{i \in [K]}\lambda(G_i)$

results.notes: Regret against ex-ante best stationary policy pi(c)=argmax_i sum_t r_{i,t}(c), expectation over contexts and algorithm randomness. Requires known context distribution.

symbols.lambda_G: maximum acyclic subgraph number lambda(G) of the common cross-learning graph G

conditions: all CL graphs G_i equal a single graph G

source.label: thm:exp3cross
source.quote: Consider the contextual bandits problem with adversarial rewards, and stochastic contexts, where all the CL graphs $G_i$ are equal to $G$ and the context distribution $\cal D$ is unknown. Let $\lambda = \lambda(G)$ ... Then \expcrossu{} (Algorithm \ref{alg:exp3C1}) incurs at most $O(\lambda K^{1/3}T^{2/3}(\log K)^{1/3})$ regret in this setting.

results.notes: Ex-ante regret against best stationary policy.

conditions: hard instance: C epochs of T/C rounds each with Bernoulli hard bandit instances per context

source.label: thm:advlb
source.quote: There exists a distribution over instances of the contextual bandit problem with complete cross-learning where any algorithm must incur a regret of at least $\Omega(\sqrt{CKT})$.

results.notes: C (number of contexts) mapped to M_ctx. Shows cross-learning does not help when both rewards and contexts are adversarial; matched by S-EXP3.

symbols.nu_2: L2 variant of the maximum acyclic subgraph number of the CL graph G (Definition def:nu_2)

conditions: all CL graphs G_i equal a fixed graph G

source.label: thm:partial-stoch-lb
source.quote: Any learning algorithm solving the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning (for a fixed CL graph $G$) and stochastic rewards and stochastic contexts must incur expected regret of $\Omega(\sqrt{\nu_2(G)KT})$, where $\nu_2(G)$ is defined in Definition \ref{def:nu_2}.

results.notes: The paper notes it also holds for adversarial rewards and stochastic contexts (benchmarks differ by at most O~(sqrt T)).

symbols.lambda_G: maximum acyclic subgraph number lambda(G) of the CL graph G

conditions: all CL graphs G_i equal a fixed graph G

source.label: thm:partial-adv-lb
source.quote: Any learning algorithm solving the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning (for a fixed CL graph $G$) with stochastic rewards and adversarial contexts must incur regret $\Omega(\sqrt{\lambda(G)KT})$

results.notes: Regret type (expected) inferred from proof ('expected regret').

bound.regime: limit as number of contexts C -> infinity

conditions: uniform context distribution over C contexts
regret against ex post best stationary policy in hindsight

source.label: theorem:expost-lower
source.quote: Under adversarial rewards and stochastic contexts, for any algorithm $\cal A$, there is an instance of the contextual bandits problem with cross-learning where $\liminf_{C\rightarrow \infty} \E[\Reg_{\post}(\cal A)] \geq T/2$.

results.notes: liminf is over the number of contexts C, not T; justifies using ex-ante benchmark.

conditions: competing bid distribution unknown; reduction from posted-price lower bound of Kleinberg and Leighton

source.label: thm:reduction
source.quote: Any algorithm must incur $\Omega(T^{2/3})$ regret for the learning to bid in first price auctions problem, even if the value of the bidder is fixed (i.e., there is only one context).

results.notes: Regret type follows the cited dynamic-pricing expected-regret lower bound.
